page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 machine family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, with hyperthreading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include any bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the e2-standard-4 sits primarily in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-bound workloads, it scored 1105.89 on stress-ng single-core and 2907.35 on multi-core, placing both metrics in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 161.16 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 24.13 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds are in the bottom 10%, while Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores also fall into the bottom 10%. However, the instance achieved an average performance rating for LLM text generation using a small 135M model, processing 104.71 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-4 offers a balanced resource allocation at a lower price point, making it a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require high-performance compute or massive memory bandwidth. Given its performance profile, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale database operations where resource demands are predictable and modest.
